approach: Add `jobs::provenance(git, change, judged, history)` in crates/athena-gate/src/jobs.rs. It judges a job's records against cross-links that Athena's own writers always leave (request record, reader invocation, defaults hash, dispatch fields, brief hash, time order). It runs only in the live gate: `jobs::check` becomes `check_records` (the old body, unchanged) plus `provenance` when `history` is None. The history walk, the frozen legacy path and `check_after_cutover` are not touched, so D111 ("commits after C0 are judged only by attribution against records") stays true, and CI re-judging of main is named as a residual and a follow-up. Every refusal is a `Rule::JobRecords` violation built by one local `fail(path, detail, repair)`; `fail` sets the path and `.in_commit(change.commit.as_deref())` like `check_records` does (jobs.rs:233-237). Its detail starts with "provenance: " and names the missing or contradicting evidence; its repair names the Athena command that writes it. R1 (any closing score or outcome of a request job, per reading): request.json exists with received_at <= reading.at; a Reader invocation with seq == invocation_seq ended at or before reading.at; if base_commit is held, defaults.toml at it hashes to defaults_sha256 (a base not held is skipped). R2 (Landed outcome only): job.json exists; the ten checked dispatch fields are present (accepted_reading, accepted_by, caps, base_commit, config_sha256, defaults_sha256, athena, driver, brief_sha256, dispatched_at); the config and defaults hashes equal the accepted reading's; `<job dir>/brief-producer.md` is in the tree and its sha256 equals brief_sha256 (new, finding 3). R4 (Landed only): the reading-before-work ordering is NOT re-defined: `provenance` calls the existing `invariant::prediction_problem` (invariant.rs:754) and reports its text. The new `dispatch_order_problem` in jobs.rs adds only what that function lacks: producers and verifiers start at or after dispatched_at; the named verifier starts at or after the latest lower-seq producer's end; outcome.at >= verifier.ended_at; verification names a Verifier invocation. No record field is added, so records.rs, reconcile.rs and history.rs are not edited.

decisions.choice: Wire the live gate through `jobs::check`: split into `check_records` (old body, unchanged) and `check`, which adds `provenance` when `history.is_none()`. The doc comments of `check` and `provenance` say plainly that `None` means a commit being made (the two live gate sites, lib.rs:357 and 372), `Some` is the frozen history walk (history.rs:255), and any future caller passing `None` on old commits must expect provenance. A short comment at the `is_none()` branch repeats this (finding 6).
decisions.reason: The live gate gains the check and every history judgment (pre-C0, non-cutover walk, legacy.rs path) stays byte-identical. No edit to lib.rs, legacy.rs, invariant.rs or history.rs, none of which is needed. A debug_assert cannot tell new commits from old, so the guard is the doc comment plus the tests that pin both sides (`the_older_build_job_in_a_non_cutover_history_is_not_refused`, and the gate wiring assertion in (c)).

rejected.why: lib.rs is not a deliverable and the None/Some split reaches the same two sites.

rejected.why: Re-judges frozen pre-C0 records that older builds wrote without dispatch fields; the sha-keyed exempt list cannot grow after the fact.
Edits invariant.rs for no gain over the None/Some split.

decisions.choice: Drop the c0..tip loop in `check_after_cutover` and its history.rs test (finding 1). Detection stays in the live gate. CI re-judging of main after C0 is listed as a residual and a follow-up, next to the athena/records question.
decisions.reason: The loop reverses D111 item 7 (docs/decisions.md:2902-2907) and the comments at history.rs:36-37 and athena.toml:152, which athena.toml being out of scope would leave stale. It judges every main commit since C0 that older builds wrote without provenance; the count that would fail cannot be measured because records/ is absent from the snapshot. A flagged commit already on main cannot be excused afterwards (is_exempt reads the parent's `[history] exempt`), so one false positive turns CI red for good. After C0, attribution already flags any main commit that no landing names, which covers hand-committed (a) and (b); (c) runs through `athena close`, which the live gate covers. The reading says 'extend the gate'.

rejected.why: Larger scope across non-deliverable docs and invariant.rs for a second line the attribution check already partly gives, with an unmeasured false-positive risk on this job's own CI.

rejected.option: Walk provenance in the non-cutover history walk
rejected.why: Refuses genuine old jobs (dispatch fields are Options, records.rs:607-633) and squash-landed jobs whose base commit is gone, with no remedy.

decisions.choice: R1 applies to any closing of a request job; R2 and R4 apply only to a Landed outcome. The checked dispatch fields are the ten listed. request_path, request_sha256, cost, tokens, note, pin and dispatch_branch are not required.
decisions.reason: `athena close` on an open job dispatched by an older build (Dropped, abandoned) must still work. Genuine dispatches write request_path, request_sha256, cost, tokens, note and pin as null (run/mod.rs:983-988; records.rs:626-633). Forgery (b) is a landing, so R2/R4 sit where it lives.

rejected.option: Require every dispatch field on every closing

decisions.choice: Landed-job ordering is defined in one place per concern: reading before dispatch and before non-reader invocations stays `prediction_problem`, which `provenance` calls on a Landed outcome; `dispatch_order_problem` in jobs.rs holds only the new orderings, and its doc comment cites `prediction_problem` (finding 4). The enforcement-map row cites both.
decisions.reason: Avoids two wordings for the same fact drifting apart. Calling it can give a second violation under Rule::JobRecords next to the landing invariant's refusal for the same fact; both name the fact, and the outcome (refused) is the same.

rejected.option: Re-implement the reading-vs-dispatch ordering inside R4

decisions.choice: A reading whose base_commit is not held is not refused. The defaults_sha256 recompute is skipped and the docs list this as a residual. The request record and reader invocation still gate every reading.
decisions.reason: A squash, gc, reset or shallow clone can drop the base, and the live gate offers no remedy. Only a held base lets defaults_sha256 be recomputed exactly (capability.rs:51).

rejected.why: It hashes `Config::reading_inputs()` (capability.rs:45), which follows the writing build's code; only compared between job.json and the reading.

decisions.choice: The verifier is ordered against the latest producer with a lower seq, not every producer. No producer is required.
decisions.reason: A retry makes a second producer start after the first verifier; a resumed kept candidate may have no producer record.

The producer and verifier still run `cargo test -p athena-core --test refusal_corpus` as a no-regression command; I cite no case ids and no result.

demonstrations.method: Run the athena-gate suite. New tests in landing_tests.rs build real temporary git repositories and call `jobs::provenance` through a new helper `provenance_of(git, rev)`, and the live `crate::gate` for the wiring. They assert the Violation list. (a) `a_job_written_by_hand_across_two_commits_is_refused`: commit 1 adds the existing all-null `opening(&HONEST)` (reading, job.json, reader invocation), where `provenance_of` is empty because nothing closes; commit 2 adds the code and `closing(fp)` (Landed). Assert violations whose detail contains 'no request record' and a missing dispatch field, and whose repair contains 'athena ask' or 'athena go'. A second variant has full genuine evidence except the request record. (b) `a_forged_landing_of_a_dispatched_job_that_never_closed_is_refused`: a genuine Read commit (request, reading, reader invocation) and Dispatch commit (full job.json plus brief-producer.md), then one forged commit adding the code and closing records. Six variants, each breaking one link: a producer started before dispatched_at; the verifier started before the producer ended; the outcome before the verifier ended; dispatched_at missing; the job's defaults hash differing from the reading's; brief-producer.md differing from brief_sha256; plus a reading recorded after dispatch (reported through prediction_problem). A control with consistent times is accepted (`..._with_consistent_times_still_passes`), recording the stated limit. (c) `a_hand_made_proposal_closed_with_athena_close_is_refused`: a reading with invented forecasts, no request record, no reader invocation, no job.json, closed by a Score plus a Dropped outcome (the shape of manage.rs:195-207). Assert 'no request record' and 'no reader invocation'; the same commit through `crate::gate(git, &change, Scope::CommitMsg)` contains a violation whose detail starts with 'provenance: '; a control with request, reader invocation, held base and matching defaults hash is accepted. (d) `the_older_build_job_in_a_non_cutover_history_is_not_refused`: the old-shape fixture with an unreachable base commit; `history_of(&git)` has no violation starting 'provenance: ', while `provenance_of` on its closing commit does refuse (the fixture triggers). Existing genuine-landing tests still pass.
demonstrations.observes: Each forged history gives at least one Rule::JobRecords Violation with detail starting 'provenance: ' that names the evidence, and carrying the commit. The controls, the genuine landing, the older-build history walk give none. All existing landing, chain, intervention and exemption tests pass, with `job_records_of` (landing_tests.rs:827) and jobs.rs `check_head` now calling `check_records`.
demonstrations.fails_without: On the base code `jobs::check` never reads the request record, the reader invocation, the dispatch fields, the brief hash, defaults.toml at the base or the invocation times, so (a), (b) and (c) fail on `!violations.is_empty()` and the `detail.contains(..)` assertions. Without the `history.is_none()` call in `check`, the Scope::CommitMsg assertion in (c) fails. If provenance ran in the plain history walk, (d) fails.
demonstrations.seam: Production entry points: `crate::jobs::provenance` via a new helper `provenance_of(git, rev)` that builds `Change::of_commit` and `Judged::new` like the existing `job_records_of` (landing_tests.rs ~823-827); `crate::gate(.., Scope::CommitMsg)` (lib.rs:337); `crate::history::check_history` via the existing `history_of`. Fixtures are real temporary git repositories from `testutil::{repo, write, commit}` and `owner_repo` (exist). Plan step 5 adds `genuine_repo` (owner_repo plus a committed defaults.toml), `genuine_reading`, `genuine_job` (all dispatch fields plus its brief file), `request_record`, and `provenance_of`. Existing: `write_records`, `opening`, `closing`, `stage_landing`, `history_of`. Nothing in the gate is stubbed.

The workspace run compiles and runs the athena-core and athena-cli suites; the lifecycle, job_plan and drain tests drive real ask/go/close through the fake driver and the production writers through the live gate, so the new links are shown to hold for Athena's own records. The xtask policy tests (M24, boundary words) and the prompt-budget test run too.

demonstrations.fails_without: Not a refusal behavior. A warning, a formatting difference, or a genuine writer's records failing the new check (a false refusal in lifecycle, job_plan or drain) fails these commands.
demonstrations.seam: Production binaries and test targets run as they are. No double. Exists.

demonstrations.method: New test `a_genuine_landing_is_not_refused` in landing_tests.rs builds the shape Athena writes with the genuine helpers. Commit 1 'Read' adds request.json, a reading with the repository's real base_commit and defaults_sha256, and the reader invocation. Commit 2 'Dispatch' adds a full job.json and brief-producer.md. Commit 3 adds the code, producer and verifier invocations in order, candidate, verification and a Landed outcome. It asserts `provenance_of` is empty for each commit and that `history_of(&git)` has no violation starting 'provenance: '. The verifier also runs the lifecycle suite (real writers, the real history shape) and the refusal corpus as a no-regression check.
demonstrations.command: cargo test -p athena-gate && cargo test -p athena-cli --test lifecycle && cargo test -p athena-core --test refusal_corpus
demonstrations.observes: No provenance violation on any genuine commit or on the walk, so refusal is by missing or contradicting evidence, not blanket. The share of the repository's real past jobs newly refused is not measured, because records/ is absent from the snapshot; the 5% is the request's estimate. The live gate sees only new commits and no earlier history is re-judged.
demonstrations.fails_without: If the check refused genuine records, `a_genuine_landing_is_not_refused` and the lifecycle tests fail. If no check existed, the criterion 1 forged tests fail.
demonstrations.seam: `provenance_of` and `history_of` on a real temporary repository with genuine-shaped helpers (added in step 5). The lifecycle suite uses its existing Fixture and fake driver with the production writers (exists).

demonstrations.method: The criterion 1 tests assert on `detail` and `repair` text, and a Grep checks the source: every violation in `jobs::provenance` is built by one local `fail(path, detail, repair)` whose detail begins with the `PROVENANCE` constant, and each call site names the missing or contradicting evidence and the Athena command that writes it. history.rs gains no refusal text because the history walk is unchanged.
demonstrations.observes: Assertions such as detail.contains('no request record'), 'no reader invocation', 'does not match defaults.toml', 'has no job.json', 'lacks dispatched_at', 'before the job was dispatched', 'before the producer invocation ended', 'before the verifier invocation ended', 'brief-producer.md', and repair.contains('athena ask') / 'athena go' / 'athena close' pass. `Grep 'provenance: ' crates/athena-gate/src/jobs.rs` lists the texts.
demonstrations.fails_without: A generic message such as 'records are not valid' fails the `contains` assertions in each forged test.
demonstrations.seam: The `Violation { detail, repair, path, commit }` values returned by `jobs::provenance`, read through `provenance_of`. Existing type; assertions added in step 5.

demonstrations.method: Content check on the diff. §16.2 of docs/design/athena-v0.md ('Records are not signed' and the table row near line 1964) and docs/enforcement.md (M27 row near line 41, 'Records are Athena's own' bullet near lines 71-78) are rewritten. They list the evidence each of the three forgeries now has to carry and name the new tests, and cite `prediction_problem` as the owner of reading-before-work. They say where the check runs (the live gate: commit-msg hook, `athena close`, every Athena commit) and the residuals: consistent, fully mimicked records still pass because nothing is signed; (b) is caught only on contradiction; job records written only to athena/records are not judged; history is not re-judged, including main commits after C0 and the non-cutover walk (D111 unchanged); a base commit not held skips the defaults hash. Every test name cited on an M27 row must be a real fn in landing_tests.rs (policy test M24).

demonstrations.method: The verifier checks that no record field or governance file changed. The provenance code reads only existing fields. The athena-data tests that hold the allow-list and the AnyRecord round-trip run unchanged since no field is added.
demonstrations.observes: The diff lists only crates/athena-gate/src/jobs.rs, crates/athena-gate/src/landing_tests.rs, docs/design/athena-v0.md, docs/enforcement.md and CHANGELOG.md. None of athena.toml, defaults.toml, .github/workflows, setup.sh, prompt files, records/, records.rs, reconcile.rs, history.rs, lib.rs or legacy.rs appears. open_questions: User: Job records written only to the athena/records branch (records-history.md stage 1) are not judged by this check, and CI does not re-judge main commits after C0 (D111 item 7 is kept). Should a follow-up job add either, with a layout adapter for the branch's root-level paths and a decision amending D111 with a remedy for a flagged commit already on main? I recommend yes for the branch, and only after the false-positive rate can be measured for main.
